title: Proactive batching thermostat: continuous profiling + safe rollout for cache-aware batching
creator: Marisol Rivera
description: Build a production-ready 'thermostat' service that continuously profiles request patterns (sequence lengths, arrival bursts, KV cache hit/miss rates, tokenization characteristics) and emits batching + cache configuration recommendations plus an automated, safe apply/rollback workflow. The goal is to reduce per-token costs and smooth tail latency without manual tuning. The thermostat combines lightweight online profiling, a rule/heuristic engine, a fast simulator/validator, and an orchestration layer for staged apply with automatic rollback triggers. This issue covers the core recommendation logic, simulator, metrics thresholding, and integration with the rollout engine (canary -> cohort -> global).
acceptance_criteria: Profiler collects per-route metrics (seq len histogram, inter-arrival times, KV cache hit-rate, average tokens per request) at 1m granularity for 90% of routes
Thermostat suggests a stable batching config (batch window ms, max batch size, batching mode: dynamic|fixed) for a given route with estimated cost delta and estimated P95 impact
Simulator validates a suggested config against a 24h workload sample and predicts token cost delta within ±7% of observed in canary

Safe apply supports canary (1% traffic), phased rollout (10%→50%→100%), and automatic rollback on predefined signals (latency SLO breach, error-rate spike, queue-length growth), with audit log entry for every change
End-to-end test demonstrates 12% median cost reduction on a synthetic bursty workload without increasing P95 beyond configured SLO
implementation_notes: Profiler runs as low-overhead sidecar aggregation into our metrics pipeline (prometheus + durable store). Store per-route compressed histograms for sequence length and arrival intervals.

Heuristics engine implements a prioritized rule set: 1) preserve P95 SLO, 2) prefer KV cache-friendly configs, 3) maximize amortized GPU token throughput. Each rule returns a soft score used by a weighted chooser.

Thermostat exposes a 'recommendation' object (route, model, recommended_batch_window_ms, recommended_max_batch, recommended_mode, expected_cost_delta, expected_latency_delta) serialized as JSON for Console and API consumers.

Simulator replays sampled requests into a fast approximation of runtime batching logic (queueing model + service time per token). Use historical kernel latency table for model variants to estimate cost.
Safety invariants: never increase max_batch beyond route-specific ceiling; require a minimum simulated confidence score before auto-apply; always run canary for customer-facing routes.

Audit and rollback: integrate with rollout-controller so that any auto-apply writes an opaque audit entry with telemetry snapshot, PR/issue ref, and Git SHA of the applying service. Rollback triggers include: latency_slo_violation_rate > 0.3% over 5m, error_rate increase > 0.5% absolute, observed cost_per_token_increase > 10%.
Instrument granular metrics needed by Console: recommended_vs_applied, simulator_confidence, predicted_cost_delta, observed_cost_delta_post_apply, rollback_reason
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit and integration tests + internal microbenchmarks (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Shadow recommendations for 10% of routes, no apply (1 week) - validate profiler coverage and simulator accuracy
Phase 2: Canary apply for non-critical routes (1% traffic) with 30m hold and automated monitoring
Phase 3: Expand to cohort rollout (10% traffic) if canary signals stable for 3 hours
Phase 4: Global apply with 10% step increments and built-in cooldown windows
Rollback policy: immediate rollback and transient blacklist for routes that trigger any hard signal during canary or cohort
test_plan: Unit tests for histogram compression and reconstruction
Simulator golden tests using recorded traffic from three production services (chat, summarization, embeddings)
Chaos test: introduce synthetic queueing delay and verify rollback triggers fire within expected window
Performance test: ensure profiler adds <1% CPU overhead on proxy nodes
E2E test in staging with Console dashboard showing predicted vs actual cost/latency after canary
notes: Tradeoffs discussed with PM: aggressive batching yields larger cost wins but increases P95 risk for tail-heavy routes. Decision: favor conservative recommendations by default and expose 'aggression' knob in Console.
Decision with infra: store only 7 days of raw histograms; rollup to weekly summaries for long-term trend analysis to keep storage costs manageable.
Open question: whether to include model quantization recommendations in thermostat v1. Deferred to next ticket to avoid scope creep.
